title: ShallowPPL: Investigating Early-Exit Logit Lens for Code Context Compression

contributions.purpose: Investigate whether the expensive full-depth perplexity scoring in LongCodeZip can be replaced by cheaper intermediate-layer scoring for code context compression.
contributions.mechanism: ShallowPPL truncates forward passes at layer L and projects intermediate representations to vocabulary space via the logit lens to approximate AMI-based code relevance scoring.
contributions.evaluation: Evaluated on Long Code Completion and RepoQA against pre-registered criteria (>=1.5x speedup, <=1.0 point quality drop).
contributions.source_quote: We propose ShallowPPL, an early-exit approach using the logit lens to approximate perplexity-based code relevance scoring at intermediate transformer layers.

contributions.purpose: Rigorously test the early-exit hypothesis under pre-committed success criteria.
contributions.mechanism: Runs evaluation with pre-registered success thresholds for speedup and quality retention.
contributions.evaluation: ShallowPPL achieves only 1.05x speedup while exceeding quality thresholds; the hypothesis does not hold (fails the >=1.5x speedup criterion).
contributions.source_quote: We conduct a rigorous evaluation with pre-registered success criteria, demonstrating that ShallowPPL fails to achieve favorable quality-speed tradeoffs.

contributions.purpose: Localize where quality is lost in the early-exit pipeline.
contributions.mechanism: Ablation studies isolating coarse function ranking and measuring per-layer quality contribution.
contributions.evaluation: Coarse function ranking is the primary bottleneck (hybrid config recovers 81% of quality gap); quality scales non-linearly with depth, with the last 2 layers contributing 3.83 percentage points.
contributions.domain: Transformer layer analysis for code relevance
contributions.source_quote: Through ablation studies, we identify that coarse function ranking is the primary quality bottleneck (hybrid configuration recovers 81% of quality gap) and that quality scales non-linearly with depth (last 2 layers contribute 3.83 percentage points).

contributions.purpose: Explain diagnostically why early-exit compression fails.
contributions.mechanism: Analysis of per-forward-pass overhead and the information content of final transformer layers.
contributions.evaluation: Per-forward-pass overhead limits speedup, and final layers encode critical code-relevance information that intermediate representations cannot approximate.
contributions.source_quote: We provide diagnostic insights explaining why early-exit fails: per-forward-pass overhead limits speedup, and final layers encode critical information for code relevance that cannot be approximated by intermediate representations.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Our work investigates whether the computational cost of LongCodeZip's AMI scoring can be reduced through early-exit inference while maintaining compression quality.

notes: Negative-result paper: the central hypothesis (early-exit logit lens can approximate full-depth AMI scoring) is refuted; ShallowPPL achieves only 1.05x speedup vs the >=1.5x pre-registered target and fails to deliver favorable quality-speed tradeoffs.
